verdict: Dell's revenue jumped 58% to a record $47.0B and profit more than tripled, powered by $16.4B of AI server sales and a $95B order backlog still to ship.

kpis.label: AI-optimized server revenue
kpis.note: +100% YoY — servers built to train and run AI models

kpis.label: AI server backlog
kpis.note: Orders booked but not yet shipped; Dell took a record $60.9B of AI orders in the quarter

segments.name: Infrastructure Solutions Group
segments.note: Servers, networking and storage — the AI engine. Revenue almost doubled to $31.8B: AI-optimized servers $16.4B (up 100%), traditional servers and networking $10.5B (up 122%) and storage $4.9B (up 26%). Operating income was $4.8B, 15.0% of its revenue.

segments.name: Client Solutions Group
segments.note: PCs and displays: $13.2B from business customers (up 22%) and $1.8B from consumers (up 7%). Operating income was $1.1B, 7.6% of its revenue.

segments.name: Corporate and other
segments.note: Small leftovers that sit outside the two groups — mainly the wind-down of reselling VMware software on its own. Down from $473M a year ago as that resale business ended.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling products and services and running the company. Rose 15% — much slower than revenue, which is how profit margins expanded.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing servers, storage and PCs, including AI systems. Rose 41% as Dell invested in its AI line-up.

otherDetail: Interest and other, net was a $254M expense. Dell reports this line only as a single net figure — mainly interest paid on its debt, partly offset by interest and other income — so there is no official split to show.

takeaways.title: AI servers drove a record quarter
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 58% to $47.0B. Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue rose 89% to $31.8B — AI-optimized servers doubled to $16.4B, traditional servers and networking rose 122% to $10.5B and storage rose 26% to $4.9B. Client Solutions (PCs) rose 20% to $15.0B. Dell raised full-year revenue guidance by $25B to $192B.

takeaways.title: Profit grew much faster than sales
takeaways.text: Operating income tripled to $5.4B (an 11.5% margin, up from 6.0%) because running costs rose only 21% while revenue rose 58%. Net income was $4.1B, up 255%, and GAAP EPS was $6.34 vs $1.70 a year ago. Dell also returned a record $4.3B to shareholders in buybacks and dividends.

takeaways.title: The order book says demand is not slowing
takeaways.text: Dell booked a record $60.9B of AI server orders in the quarter and ended it with a $95B backlog — orders taken but not yet delivered or counted as revenue. That backlog, not just this quarter's sales, is why full-year AI server revenue guidance rose to $74B.

footerNote: Amounts are reported in $M and tie exactly. Segment revenues are from the 10-Q segment note and sum to total net revenue.
follow100Note: The two segment groups plus Corporate and other ($155M) sum to total net revenue. Operating expenses are the GAAP figures, which include stock-based pay and amortization.
